notes.body:
Shop platform: high-level design

How the web client, catalog-svc, inventory-svc and order-intake fit together, and which subsystem owns which data. A reading aid for the HLD review, not a deployment map.

Scope

  • In: the Shop and Catalog subsystems, their data stores, the client entry points.
  • Out: payments (own design), batch jobs, the admin tools.
    • Admin tools get their own document.

Subsystems

SubsystemOwnsDataEntry points
Catalogproducts, reviewsmongodb:catalog-dbin.get.products.id.reviews, in.get.products
Stockavailability, reservationsread through inventory-svcin.get.products.id.availability
Ordersorders, payments hand-offpostgres:orders-dbin.submit

Architecture

Calls between the subsystems, as a Mermaid sequence diagram:

sequenceDiagram
  participant W as web client
  participant C as catalog-svc
  participant D as catalog-db
  W->>C: GET /products/{id}/reviews
  C->>D: find reviews by productId
  D-->>C: Review[]
  C-->>W: 200 Review[]

Key decisions

  1. Catalog owns product and review data. Orders reads Catalog only through its API, never its DB (see GET /products/{id}/reviews, step 1).
  2. Cross-subsystem events go over SNS/SQS, not direct calls.
  3. Reviews are read straight from MongoDB with no cache. Revisit if in.get.products.id.reviews shows up in the latency report.

Example: reading reviews

The flow catalog-svc · reviews is the smallest example of a read that ends in a store. Its flow doc has the callouts.

GET /products/42/reviews
  -> catalog-svc: find({ productId: 42 })
  <- 200 [ { rating: 5, text: "..." } ]

Constraints

  • No new datastore without a review.
  • Every cross-subsystem call carries a correlation id.

notes.author: Dana Levi
notes.body:
Purpose

Returns the reviews of one product. Read-only: one find on catalog-db.

Callouts

find on reviews is the only data-store access. The endpoint latency is this call.

The product id is not validated before the find, so a bad id returns an empty list, not a 404.

No pagination: every review of a hot product comes back in one find.

How it works

  1. step 1 The client calls GET /products/{id}/reviews.
  2. step 2 catalog-svc runs find({ productId }) on the reviews collection.
  3. step 3 The list goes back as 200 Review[].

call.what: Public entry. Checks the session only; the product id goes to the find unchecked.
call.watch: The id is not validated here.

call.what: Reads every review of the product by id. The reviews collection is indexed on productId.
call.contract: find({ productId }) → Review[] · unknown id → [] · sorted by createdAt desc
